title: SDK flow resilience handbook: streaming tool contracts (WIP)
body:
Status: WIP — purpose is to consolidate a lightweight, operational playbook for SDK-side streaming, tool-calling, and structured-output resilience. This is aimed at product + SDK + integrations teams; not final API copy.

Background and motivation:
- We ship streaming responses, tool calls, and structured JSON outputs. In real networks and mixed client capabilities we get partial responses, dropped frames, duplicate tool invocations, and schema regressions.
- Current ad-hoc fixes live in SDK layers and customer integrations; we need a coherent surface and observable contract so clients can implement consistent resume, dedup, and fallback behavior.

Problem statements (short):
1) Partial/ambiguous structured output: streams can emit valid JSON fragments, interleaved plain text, or final JSON that violates expected schema. Clients either crash on parse or silently accept bad data.
2) Tool call idempotency & duplication: network retries and client replays cause tool backends to see repeated invocations without a clean de-duplication key and semantic lifecycle (start/commit/abort).
3) Resume and backpressure ergonomics: mobile and edge clients need resume tokens + compact checkpoints to avoid re-generating entire sequences after a disconnection.
4) Observability gap: telemetry events are inconsistent across SDKs; product cannot correlate partial-response regressions to model or runtime variants.

Goals (measurable):
- Define a minimal, cross-language SDK contract for streaming structured output + tool calls.
- Reduce duplicated tool invocations due to client retries by 80% within first rollout (tracked via HOSTED-1423).
- Provide a resume token + compact checkpoint model that reduces bytes retransmitted on reconnect by >= 60% for mobile use cases.
- Standardize telemetry keys so post-hoc analysis can attribute schema regressions to model rollouts.

Non-goals:
- Rework of server-side model grammars or forcing model output formats. Server can provide hints but we avoid hard server-only migrations in this PRD.
- Complex transactional guarantees across third-party tools (we define pragmatic best-effort semantics, not distributed ACID).

Personas:
- Frontend mobile engineer (low-bandwidth, intermittent connectivity) — cares about resume tokens, small checkpoint payloads, simple APIs.
- Backend integrator (server-side BFF) — wants idempotent tool-call hooks and durable commit signals.
- SDK maintainer — needs ergonomic primitives to expose to customers, with small breaking change surface.

Success metrics (initial):
- SDK crash rate for streaming parse errors < 2% of active sessions in first 30 days.
- Measured duplicate tool-call incidents drop 80% in telemetry within 45 days.
- Average bytes re-sent on reconnect reduced by 60% for instrumented mobile flows.

Proposed surface (high-level):
1) Stream envelope: every stream event is a compact JSONL envelope (one envelope per line when streaming over sockets/HTTP chunking). Envelope fields:
   - event_type: chunk | tool_call | tool_result | checkpoint | finalize | heartbeat
   - seq: monotonically increasing int (server-assigned within session)
   - session_id: opaque string (session scope)
   - resume_token: optional string (opaque token for reconnect)
   - payload: string (for chunk/heartbeat) OR object (for structured payloads/tool_result)
   - schema_version: optional string (helps client choose parser)

   Notes: keep envelope tiny. Clients must tolerate unknown fields. Server guarantees seq monotonicity but not contiguity when fallbacks occur.

2) Checkpoint & resume semantics:
   - Checkpoints are opt-in events emitted periodically or at important boundaries. Checkpoint payloads contain: { seq, resume_token, small_kv: {last_action_id, partial_schema_anchor}} encoded as compact base64 to minimize bytes.
   - On reconnect clients present the last resume_token; server attempts a fast-path reconnect (replay deltas from next seq) or falls back to a full session snapshot.
   - Guaranteed: resume_token validity window is at least 5 minutes for hosted cheap path; Dedicated/Private deployments may configure longer TTLs.

3) Tool-call lifecycle and idempotency:
   - Tool_call envelope: includes call_id (client-provided UUID) and idempotency_key (optional, recommended).
   - Server echoes tool_call events into control-plane logs and includes a tool_ack envelope once the runtime accepted the invocation (tool_ack contains call_id, assigned_tool_instance, and opt-in dedupe_hint).
   - Tool_result envelope contains call_id and result payload. If a client retries with same idempotency_key, server should dedupe if dedupe_hint is present.
   - Best-effort rules: server will never delete dedupe records within 1 minute; recommended 15 minutes for most workloads. Longer TTLs are an opt-in config.

4) Structured output gating and schema versioning:
   - Schema_version in envelopes is small string (eg: v1.2). SDKs ship lightweight validators for stable schema subsets; if client sees an unknown schema_version it should: (a) buffer raw payload and surface a warning telemetry event, (b) fallback to text rendering mode for display.
   - Server to include a lightweight schema_anchor hash in checkpoints indicating the expected top-level fields. Clients can decide to enforce or degrade gracefully.

5) SDK ergonomics (surface proposals):
   - High-level APIs: streaming.subscribe(sessionId, opts) returns a StreamHandle exposing: on('chunk', cb), on('toolCall', cb), on('checkpoint', cb), resume(lastResumeToken).
   - Low-ceremony tool invocation: StreamHandle.invokeTool(name, {input, idempotencyKey?}) -> returns a Promise that resolves on tool_result or rejects on explicit abort. SDK auto-manages call_id and attaches a short-lived idempotency key if not supplied.
   - Default behavior: SDKs should automatically emit resume_token checkpoints every 4–8 seconds for mobile, and allow opt-in for coarse-grained checkpoints for desktop.
   - Backpressure/flow-control: provide a credit-based mechanism for clients (client sends credit X to server; server will not exceed outstanding chunks > X). Default credit=16.

Telemetry / observability (must-haves):
- Events standardized across SDKs: streaming.open, streaming.close, streaming.resume_attempt, streaming.resume_success, tool.invoke, tool.ack, tool.result, schema.mismatch, checkpoint.emitted, checkpoint.resumed, duplicate-tool-detected.
- Each event must include session_id, seq (if applicable), model_variant, infra_node (when available), sdk_version, network_rtt_ms estimate.
- Aggregate dashboards: duplicate tool-call rate by model_variant, streaming parse error rate by schema_version, resume success rate by region.

Security & privacy notes:
- resume_tokens must be opaque, short-lived, and not leak PII. Treat them as bearer tokens for session rehydration only.
- Tool input/output may include PII; clients should be provided a best-practice note to scrub or mark tool_calls with sensitivity flags.

Compatibility & migration path:
- Backward compat: server will accept legacy plain-text chunks without envelope; SDKs in compatibility mode will reconstruct envelopes heuristically but emit schema.mismatch telemetry.
- Rollout plan: start with SDK Canary in Node/TS and Python (alpha), toggle server-side option host.stream.envelope=true for 10% of traffic. After 2 weeks of telemetry, expand to 50% then GA.

Operational playbook (appendix):
- On schema.mismatch spike: temporarily route affected sessions to conservative text-only model variant, create incident with SRE and product.
- On resume failures: inspect resume_success_rate dashboard, correlate to infra_node and model_variant; if resume tokens frequently expire, increase TTL for Dedicated customers as a stopgap.

Open questions / tradeoffs (for sync):
- How large can checkpoint payloads be before we break low-bandwidth flows? (proposal: 1KB max per checkpoint)
- Do we require client idempotency_keys or can server generate dedupe stable tokens from call fingerprints?
- How to handle tool-call side-effects that are non-idempotent (billing webhooks, external writes)? Recommend: server emits tool_ack early and recommends clients use confirm/commit semantics for destructive effects.

Next steps / owners:
- Draft RFC for envelope format and checkpoint encoding (owner: Marco Li) — target RFC by 2026-03-24.
- Implement Node + Python SDK beta helpers: subscribe API + auto-checkpoint (owner: Danielle Kim) — spike 2 weeks.
- Instrument telemetry keys and add dashboards (owner: Evan Brooks + Observability) — dashboard PR by 2026-04-07.

Notes to reviewer:
- This doc assumes server can emit deterministic seq numbers and small resume tokens. If serving-runtime constraints prevent that, we need a plan B (opaque monotonic checkpoints with client-side heuristics).
- Please comment inline with specific SDK ergonomics that feel heavy for your language (callback-heavy vs promise/async-first).

Hand-off references and tickets: see linked_artifacts above; primary tracking is HOSTED-1423.

-- Aisha
